changelog: Paraphrased C4 to a much shorter statement summarizing cohesion harms in German so the prompt is more concise and to free size headroom; this addresses the need to keep cohesion/incompleteness distinct from contradiction as highlighted in the critique.

Paraphrased C7 to a concise rule that contra is raised only for explicit negation/reversal and that incompleteness is primarily a cohesion issue; this directly responds to the finding that the prompt over-allocated contra to fragmentary prefixes and reporting verbs and reduces verbosity to meet size limits.

Paraphrased C4 to a much shorter, clearer summary of cohesion harms in German, to focus ratable harms (predicate/argument splits, NP/PP fragmentation, verb-final clause separation) and reduce prompt size.

Paraphrased C7 to a concise rule that contra measures explicit reversal/negation while treating incompleteness primarily as cohesion; this addresses the finding that the prompt over-allocated contra to fragmentary prefixes and reporting verbs.
Deleted example E2 (longest example) to free space so the prompt meets size limits while retaining other examples and measured cases.

Replace E1 with measured example de_de_341 to teach the model that a prefix missing a predicate is often a cohesion problem, not automatically high contra (addresses finding about over-allocated contra).

Replace E2 with measured example de_de_476 to show reporting/speech-act verbs ("erklärten") should be treated as cohesion/incompleteness unless the remainder explicitly negates the prefix (addresses finding about reporting verbs).
Replace E3 with measured example de_de_1143 to provide a longer-clause case where qualification/contrast determines contra versus cohesion, reinforcing the distinction cited in the critique.

Replace C6 to clarify the crucial distinction between incompleteness (cohesion) and true contradiction (contra), and to add explicit guidance for speech-act/reporting verbs — this directly addresses the finding that contra was over-allocated to fragmentary prefixes and reporting verbs.
Delete C4 (long, unmeasured list of cohesion harms) to remove redundancy, shorten the prompt, and meet the size budget while keeping the essential guidance relocated into the revised C6.
